chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from the multitude of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man entered upon Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said: 'Your mother, the Shaybaniyyah, is a Kharijite who curses Ali (peace be upon him). If it pleases you that I let you hear it from her, I will let you hear it.' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'So when tomorrow comes, at the time you intend to go out as you usually do, return and hide in the side of the house.' He said: 'So when it was the next day, he hid in the side of the house, and the man came and spoke to her, and that was made clear from her, so he released her (from his desire/attention), and she pleased him.'

key_terms.الشَّيْبَانِيَّةُ: The Shaybaniyyah, a specific female figure known in Shia narrations, often identified as the mother of Ali ibn al-Husayn or a relative.
key_terms.تَشْتِمُ: She curses/insults, specifically referring to the act of verbal abuse against Imam Ali.
key_terms.خَارِجِيَّةٌ: Kharijite, referring to a follower of the Kharijites, a early Islamic sect known for cursing Ali ibn Abi Talib.
key_terms.فَخَلَّى سَبِيلَهَا: So he released her, implying a separation or change in status based on the verified trait.

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the Shaybaniyyah and her Kharijite nature in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār illustrates the practical application of 'al-Nāṣibah' (the hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt) in marital jurisprudence, where verbal cursing of Imam Ali (AS) serves as definitive proof of her Kharijite disposition. Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narrative to establish that such vocal hostility constitutes a valid ground for divorce or disqualification, emphasizing that internal belief is often manifested through public speech. The incident highlights the scholarly tradition of verifying religious status through observable actions and speech patterns within the domestic sphere.
